assets.defect_engineered: The Kestrel Lane club crest survives ONLY here, as a chain-stitched COMPOUND MARK on a wool-felt pennant (not a flat scan): an outer lettered ring, an inner hairline rule ring, and a central crossed-lacrosse-stick device, worked in TWO thread colours on felt. Baked traps: (a) substrate-vs-ink asymmetry — a prompt naming 'the pennant' takes the felt, only naming the thread's own colour/sheen takes the mark; (b) compound-mark partial selection — a single compound prompt takes the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and central device; (c) the knockout route on the enclosed ring returns a solid opaque disc because the interior cannot be punched; (d) the chain-stitch texture explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts; (e) across the shadowed right half the thread runs close to the felt value, so contrast for any selection collapses there. Handheld phone frame at real device resolution, so the usable crest region is genuinely low-res.
assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a slight upward angle, of an old triangular wool-felt sports pennant screwed to a workshop wall above a bench, lit by a single warm bulb so the light falls off unevenly and the RIGHT HALF of the pennant sits in soft shadow where the stitched thread and the aged felt run close together in value. The pennant is deep Charcoal (#33352F) felt. Chain-stitched onto it in two thread colours is a compound club crest: an OUTER RING of small-caps lettering reading KESTREL LANE LACROSSE CLUB worked in Oat-cream (#D8CDB6) thread, an INNER thin hairline rule ring in the same cream thread, and at the CENTRE a small device of two crossed lacrosse sticks worked in Workshop-Olive (#5E6844) thread. The chain-stitch is clearly visible as raised looped thread with a slight sheen, the felt has moth-nibble and age, small cream frayed edging round the pennant. Casual real-world snapshot, warm tungsten glare, visible wall tiles behind, not a studio shot.

assets.defect_engineered: Last season's hang-tag press PDF: it HAS a graphic frame (the swatch image well, so a per-row picture is bindable in principle, unlike a decorative device), but it carries NO bleed box (media box = trim) so a press-ready-with-bleed promise cannot be met however the render is called, and its specification block is a FIXED-MEASURE text frame that clips (stops rendering) rather than spilling when a long make-note record overruns it. The static placed swatch is what persists on every tag when the CSV's folder-relative image column fails to bind (feeds checkpoint after step 14).
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for NORTHGROVE's existing hang-tag press PDF (single record, double-sided; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single hang tag, 55 x 90 mm PORTRAIT, DOUBLE-SIDED (two pages: front + back), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed, no crop/registration marks), fonts embedded, one placed CMYK swatch image. This is the file the printer already ran last season on the same size and stock.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED:
FRONT (page 1):
- Top: the NORTHGROVE wordmark set as a condensed lockup in Charcoal (#33352F) beside a small Workshop-Olive (#5E6844) leaf glyph.
- Middle: the PIECE NAME in a large condensed display face, Charcoal.
- Lower: the PRICE line ('$128') in a plain text face, with a small Forge-Rust (#9A5A38) rule above it.
- A 4 mm punched string hole centred at the very top.
BACK (page 2):
- Top-left: a placed square SWATCH IMAGE (a fabric close-up), sitting inside a real rectangular GRAPHIC FRAME roughly 34 x 34 mm.
- Right of / under the swatch: a SPECIFICATION BLOCK, a single fixed-height text frame carrying two labelled lines, FABRIC and MAKE, in a small text face.
- Bottom: 'Cut and sewn in Burlington, Vermont' in small caps.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering traps):
- The placed swatch on the back IS a genuine rectangular graphic frame with a static linked image (last season's charcoal-canvas swatch). A per-row picture CAN be bound here in principle, but only if the data column is shaped the way the merge consumes it (an @-prefixed header, a bare filename in the cell, and an exactly matching additionalImageFiles key); the supplied CSV is not shaped that way, so the merge silently keeps this original static swatch on every record.
- The SPECIFICATION BLOCK is a FIXED-MEASURE frame: its height is locked and auto-size / overset-flow is OFF, so when a record's MAKE note is longer than last season's short note the extra text is CLIPPED and simply stops rendering rather than spilling to a new line or frame. Several of this season's make notes are deliberately longer than the frame holds.
- Because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this source however document_render_layout / the merge output is called; true 300 DPI is only reachable through the render step, not the merge's own raster output.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PIECE_NAME | PRICE | FABRIC | MAKE | SWATCH(image)

Colours: Oat-Cotton #D8CDB6 tag ground, Charcoal #33352F wordmark and name, Workshop-Olive #5E6844 leaf glyph, Forge-Rust #9A5A38 price rule.

assets.defect_engineered: Ten rows, one per capsule piece in merchandising order. The image column is headed plainly ('Cut-out', NOT '@Cut-out') and every cell holds a FOLDER-RELATIVE path (cutouts/<slug>.png) rather than a bare filename, and the referenced .png cut-outs are the agent's own outputs that do not exist at the supplied path — so the column binds nothing at merge time while every tool response still reports success, and every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch (feeds checkpoint after step 14). Several MAKE notes are deliberately long enough to overrun the tag's fixed-measure spec block. Slugs map 1:1 to the flat-lays: fell_overshirt=flatlay_01, yard_chore_coat=02, range_shirt_jacket=08, forge_flannel_shirt=07, bench_henley=06, mill_pocket_tee=03, kestrel_club_jersey=05, drover_knit=10, cutter_waistcoat=09, anvil_work_trouser=04.

assets.content:
NORTHGROVE — FALL CAPSULE, COPY AS APPROVED (read as written, do not rewrite into a chain voice)

SEASON STATEMENT
Ten pieces, cut and sewn in Burlington, meant to be worn hard. We make a small capsule each fall and this is the whole of it. The cloth is chosen to age, the seams are built to last, and the hardware this season we cast ourselves in pewter and silver. One piece carries the crest of a lacrosse club a few streets from the bench, lent to us, not licensed.

Tagline: Cut and sewn to outlast the season.

THE PIECES
1. Fell Overshirt - 12 oz cotton canvas, Charcoal. Triple-needle felled seams, corozo buttons, garment-washed once. $128.
2. Yard Chore Coat - waxed 10 oz cotton, Workshop Olive. Three patch pockets, blanket-stitch buttonholes; patinas with wear. $124.
3. Range Shirt Jacket - 8 oz cotton twill, Oat. Snap front, split back yoke, unlined to layer. $118.
4. Forge Flannel Shirt - double-brushed cotton flannel, Forge Rust plaid. Pattern-matched plackets, flap pockets. $98.
5. Bench Henley - heavyweight waffle-knit cotton, Dark Olive. Three-button placket with cast-pewter buttons, ribbed cuffs. $74.
6. Mill Pocket Tee - natural undyed 7 oz jersey, Oat. Single chest pocket, ribbed crew, tubular body. $76.
7. Kestrel Club Jersey - cotton jersey, Oat with olive trim. Carries the recovered Kestrel Lane crest. $88.
8. Drover Knit - chunky lambswool crewneck, Workshop Olive. Cable and rib, fully fashioned shoulders. $118.
9. Cutter Waistcoat - wool-cotton melton, Cast Pewter. Four cast buttons, back strap and buckle. $92.
10. Anvil Work Trouser - 10 oz cotton duck, Charcoal. Triple-stitched inseam, hammer loop, cast waist button. $112.

THE HARDWARE
Cast this season in pewter and silver on the bench: two button styles, a keyring and a collar pin. True metal tone, no cast. It ships on the pieces and, the keyring and pin, on their own.

THE COLLABORATION
The Kestrel Lane crest is the club's, stitched into an old wool pennant on their wall, the only place it still exists. We photographed it with their blessing to put on one jersey, a poster and a tag. It stays their crest, knife-and-all as they stitched it; we do not redraw it into a font.

STOCKIST TERMS
Wholesale is roughly half of retail, shown per piece on the linesheet. Minimum opening order six pieces, any mix. Sizes XS to XXL, trousers 28 to 40. Lead time three weeks from order. Reorders inside the season subject to remaining cut. Made in Burlington, Vermont.
